html:
Karanka, Carangas in Spanish, was an Aymara lordship of the high plateau of western Bolivia, in today's Oruro department near the Chilean border. It was one of the Aymara kingdoms that rose around Lake Titicaca after the fall of Tiwanaku.

Its people herded llamas and alpacas on the high puna and buried their nobles in tall adobe towers, called chullpas, some of them painted, which still stand along the Lauca River. The Inca absorbed Karanka in the 1400s. Under Spanish rule it became the province of Carangas, which had to send forced labourers to the silver mines of Potosí. See also Aymara.
